cards.text: Jesus is on His way to Jerusalem, passing between Samaria and Galilee. That's a LONG walk, friend. The longest trip I ever took was from the counter to the back of a junk drawer, and I still needed a nap.
He walks into one of the villages, and ten lepers come to meet Him. Under the law, a person with leprosy had to live alone, outside the camp (Leviticus 13:46).

cards.question: The ten lepers walk right up to Jesus to meet Him.
The ten lepers stand at a distance. How do they get Jesus' attention?

answers.text: They raise their voices and shout
They send a friend to bring Him
They wave until He comes over

cards.question: The ten lepers call out to Jesus and ask Him for ___.

cards.text: And Jesus sees them. I spent years in the back of a junk drawer waiting for somebody to notice me, so trust me, friend. That part right there? That's BIG.

cards.question: When Jesus sees the ten lepers, what does He tell them to do?

answers.text: Go show yourselves to the priests
Go wash seven times in the Jordan
Come close and touch My cloak

cards.text: Under the law, a leper was brought to the priest on the day of his cleansing (Leviticus 14:2). And Jesus sends them off while they're STILL lepers, like heading to the bank with a check that hasn't even come in the mail!

cards.question: The ten lepers are cleansed while they're on their way to the priests.
One of the ten sees that he's healed. What does he do?

answers.text: He hurries on to the priests
He goes home to his family

cards.question: The healed man comes back praising God quietly, under his breath.
The healed man reaches Jesus and falls facedown at His feet.

cards.text: He's not there to ask for anything. He's there to say thank you. Then Luke adds one more detail about who this man is.

cards.question: Jesus is passing between Samaria and Galilee. Luke says where the healed man who came back is from. What is he?
Jesus asks where the other ___ are, since all ___ were cleansed.
Jesus asks if no one was found to return and give ___ to God except this foreigner.

cards.text: All ten cleansed, and ONE comes back to say thank you. Now, I'm not pointing my mustache at anybody. I got a brand new life on a cookie planet, and some mornings I'm halfway through my first batch before I remember to say thank you! Then Jesus tells the man, "Rise and go…"

cards.question: Jesus tells the Samaritan to rise and go. What does Jesus say has made him well?

findings.problem: This is the first time Jesus shows up, and the card doesn't say simply who He is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: "And Jesus sees them." / "I spent years..." / "That part right there?" / "That's BIG."

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The card gives away card 9's answer. It says a leper goes to the priest on the day of his cleansing, and that Jesus sends them off while they're STILL lepers. The check joke then implies the healing arrives after they leave. Together these tell the baker the cleansing happens on the way.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Luke shows up here for the first time ("Then Luke adds one more detail"), and the card doesn't say who he is.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: Earlier cards already gave away both blanks. Cards 2 and 3 say there are ten lepers, and card 10 says one of the ten came back. That leaves "nine" and "ten" as simple arithmetic on facts already told, so the card tests nothing new.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences and three beats: a recap of verses 17-18, the thank-you joke, and Jesus telling the man to rise and go.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: The opening line, "All ten cleansed, and ONE comes back to say thank you," recaps what cards 10, 15 and 16 already covered.
"His faith" and "His praise" are both things about the man. "The priests" is a group of people, so it isn't the same kind of answer.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.
